tool.name: lab_strain_watch
tool.description: identity check of a sequenced laboratory yeast strain: strain, mating type, markers, mtDNA, tool elements
tool.command:
#import re #set $pipeline = $__tool_directory__ + '/..' set -o pipefail && ## apptainer runs the processes of the pipeline (requirement of the tool, or module loaded by the job configuration of the server) command -v apptainer > /dev/null || { echo 'ERROR: apptainer not found in the PATH of the Galaxy job' >&2; exit 1; } && ## strain identity database of the server if [[ ! -d "\${LSW_DB_PATH:-}" ]]; then echo "ERROR: the LSW_DB_PATH variable of the Galaxy job must be set by the Galaxy administrators to the db folder of a clone of https://github.com/lab-strain-watch/yeast_db (current value: '\${LSW_DB_PATH:-}')" >&2; exit 1; fi && ## nextflow.config uses ./bin/... paths (template_rmd_path), relative to the launch folder (the job working folder) ln -s '$pipeline/bin' bin && ## sample name: name of the folder of the sample files, used as sample name by the pipeline (fastq_name of main.nf) #if $input.input_type == 'files': #set $first = str($input.seq_files[0].element_identifier) #elif $input.input_type == 'paired': #set $first = str($input.forward.element_identifier) #elif $input.input_type == 'paired_collection': #set $first = str($input.pair.name) #end if #if $input.input_type != 'accession': #set $sample_name = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+', '_', str($input.sample_name).strip()).strip('_') #if not $sample_name: ## name of the first dataset, without its extensions and mate suffix: sample_R1.fastq.gz -> sample #set $sample_name = re.sub(r'(?i)(\.(gz|bz2|zip|fastq|fq|fastqsanger|fasta|fa|fna|fas|fsa|seq|txt|gb|gbk|gbff|genbank|embl|dat|bam|sam|cram))+\Z', '', $first) #set $sample_name = re.sub(r'[._]R?[12]\Z', '', $sample_name) #set $sample_name = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+', '_', $sample_name).strip('_') #end if #if not $sample_name: #set $sample_name = 'sample' #end if #end if ## input files to stage in the job folder: [folder, dataset, name of the dataset] #set $to_stage = [] #if $input.input_type == 'files': #for $f in $input.seq_files: #silent $to_stage.append(['sample/' + $sample_name, $f, str($f.element_identifier)]) #end for #elif $input.input_type == 'paired': #silent $to_stage.append(['sample/' + $sample_name, $input.forward, $sample_name + '_R1']) #silent $to_stage.append(['sample/' + $sample_name, $input.reverse, $sample_name + '_R2']) #elif $input.input_type == 'paired_collection': #silent $to_stage.append(['sample/' + $sample_name, $input.pair.forward, $sample_name + '_R1']) #silent $to_stage.append(['sample/' + $sample_name, $input.pair.reverse, $sample_name + '_R2']) #end if #if $data.cram.cram_source == 'own': #silent $to_stage.append(['references/cram_reference', $data.cram.cram_fasta, 'cram_reference']) #end if ## staging: hard link (no copy of big read files), or copy if the dataset is on another file system. ## File name: dataset name without its extensions, plus the extension of its Galaxy datatype (.gz and .bz2 are read from the name) #set $staged = [] #for $item in $to_stage: #set $folder = $item[0] #set $f = $item[1] #set $ext = str($f.ext) #set $comp = '' #if $ext.endswith('.gz'): #set $comp = '.gz' #elif $ext.endswith('.bz2'): #set $comp = '.bz2' #end if #if 'bam' in $ext: #set $suffix = 'bam' #elif $ext in ['sam', 'cram', 'zip']: #set $suffix = $ext #elif $ext.startswith('fastq'): #set $suffix = 'fastq' + $comp #elif $ext.startswith('genbank'): #set $suffix = 'gb' + $comp #elif $ext.startswith('embl'): #set $suffix = 'embl' + $comp #else: #set $suffix = 'fasta' + $comp #end if #set $stem = re.sub(r'(?i)(\.(gz|bz2|zip|fastq|fq|fastqsanger|fasta|fa|fna|fas|fsa|seq|txt|faa|gb|gbk|gbff|genbank|embl|dat|bam|sam|cram))+\Z', '', $item[2]) #set $stem = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+', '_', $stem).strip('._') #if not $stem: #set $stem = 'seq' #end if #set $name = $stem + '.' + $suffix #if ($folder + '/' + $name) in $staged: #set $name = str(len($staged)) + '_' + $name #end if #silent $staged.append($folder + '/' + $name) mkdir -p '$folder' && { ln -- '$f' '$folder/$name' 2> /dev/null || cp -- '$f' '$folder/$name'; } && #end for ## nextflow.config of the job (copied by the pipeline into the reports folder): values of the form, then of the optional parameter file, then those of the server python3 '$__tool_directory__/fill_config.py' --template '$pipeline/nextflow.config' --locked '$__tool_directory__/locked_params.txt' --galaxy-inputs '$form_values' --galaxy-ignore input_type,sample_name,accession,cram_source,tables,zip #if $advanced.params: --values '$advanced.params' #end if #if $input.input_type == 'accession': --set 'fastq_path=$input.accession' #else: --set "fastq_path=\$PWD/sample/$sample_name" #end if #if $data.cram.cram_source == 'own': --set "cram_reference=\$PWD/references/cram_reference/cram_reference.fasta" #end if --set "db_path=\$LSW_DB_PATH" --set system_exec=local --set "apptainer_local_images=\${LSW_APPTAINER_CACHE:?the LSW_APPTAINER_CACHE variable must be set by the Galaxy administrators (folder of the apptainer images)}" --set "cluster_runOptions=\${LSW_APPTAINER_OPTIONS:---no-home --bind /pasteur}" --set "out_path_ini=\$PWD/results" --set result_folder_name=lab_strain_watch --cpus "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --memory-mb "\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-}" -o nextflow.config && export NXF_HOME="\$PWD/.nextflow_home" && export NXF_OFFLINE=true && export APPTAINER_TMPDIR="\${APPTAINER_TMPDIR:-\$PWD/apptainer_tmp}" && mkdir -p "\$APPTAINER_TMPDIR" && nextflow -C nextflow.config run '$pipeline/main.nf' -work-dir work -ansi-log false && ## outputs: the report.html dataset carries the whole result folder (its links work in Galaxy, its download is a zip of the folder) results_dir=\$(ls -d results/lab_strain_watch_*) && cp "\$results_dir/report.html" '$report' && mkdir -p '$report.extra_files_path' && cp -r "\$results_dir"/. '$report.extra_files_path' && ## no strain_identity_report.html without strain panel in the database (warning of the run) if [[ -f "\$results_dir/strain_identity_report.html" ]]; then cp "\$results_dir/strain_identity_report.html" '$strain_report'; else echo 'No strain identity report

No strain identity report was produced: see the warnings at the end of the report of the "report and result folder" dataset (no strain panel in the database of the Galaxy server).

' > '$strain_report'; fi && #if $output_options.zip: (cd results && python3 -m zipfile -c '$results_zip' "\$(basename "\$results_dir")") && #end if #if $output_options.tables: mkdir tables && cp "\$results_dir"/tsv/*.tsv tables/ && #end if echo "result folder: \$results_dir"

param.name: input_type
param.label: Sample sequences (fastq_path)
param.help: Sequences of a single sample, reads or assembly. All the files are analyzed together as one sample.
param.option: Paired-end reads: forward and reverse files

param.name: seq_files
param.label: Sequence file(s)
param.help: One or several files of the sample (or a list collection): FASTQ, FASTA, GenBank or EMBL (plain, .gz or .bz2), BAM, SAM, CRAM, or a zip archive of FASTQ, FASTA, GenBank or EMBL files. The format is recognized from the content. Paired files are recognized by the _1/_2 or _R1/_R2 suffix of their dataset names, e.g., sample_R1.fastq.gz and sample_R2.fastq.gz.

param.name: sample_name
param.label: Sample name
param.help: Name of the sample in the reports: letters, digits, _ and - only. Empty: the name of the first dataset, without its extensions and mate suffix (_1, _R1...).

param.name: forward
param.label: Forward reads (R1)
param.help: FASTQ or FASTA, plain, .gz or .bz2.

param.name: reverse
param.label: Reverse reads (R2)
param.help: FASTQ or FASTA, plain, .gz or .bz2, in the order of the forward reads.

param.name: sample_name
param.label: Sample name
param.help: Name of the sample in the reports: letters, digits, _ and - only. Empty: the name of the forward dataset, without its extensions and mate suffix (_1, _R1...).

param.name: pair
param.label: Paired collection
param.help: Collection of the forward and reverse reads, FASTQ or FASTA, plain, .gz or .bz2.

param.name: sample_name
param.label: Sample name
param.help: Name of the sample in the reports: letters, digits, _ and - only. Empty: the name of the collection.

param.name: accession
param.label: Run accession
param.help: Run accession of SRA (SRR...), ENA (ERR...) or DDBJ (DRR...), downloaded by fastq-dump during the run and used as sample name. Warning: this requires an internet access from the computing node of the Galaxy job, which some Galaxy servers do not give. Otherwise, import the reads into the history first (e.g., with the Galaxy tool Faster Download and Extract Reads in FASTQ, if available) and use the Sequence file(s) option.

validator.message: A run accession, e.g., SRR26617475, is expected

param.name: seq_kind
param.label: Kind of sequences (seq_kind)
param.help: reads: sequencing reads, short or long (long reads are cut into pieces for the bowtie2 alignments, see shred_max_length). assembly: contigs, scaffolds or a whole genome sequence. The depth thresholds kmer_min_depth and marker_min_depth are then set to 1, since an assembly has one copy of each sequence, and the depths of the tool elements and of the native marker genes no longer measure copy number.
param.option: reads: sequencing reads, short or long
assembly: contigs, scaffolds or a whole genome sequence

param.name: seq_molecule
param.label: Molecule (seq_molecule)
param.help: RNA for RNA-seq reads or direct RNA reads: the analysis is the same, U is read as T, but the report warns that depths then follow gene expression, and that a strain site or a marker gene that is not expressed is reported as not covered.

param.name: cram_source
param.label: Reference of a CRAM sample (cram_reference)
param.help: Only for a CRAM sample: the FASTA reference it was compressed against.
param.option: None (NULL): samtools finds the reference from its checksum, which needs internet access
FASTA reference of the CRAM file

param.name: cram_fasta
param.label: FASTA reference of the CRAM file

param.name: shred_max_length
param.label: Maximal length of the aligned sequences (shred_max_length)
param.help: Sequences longer than this (long reads, contigs) are cut into pieces of shred_length bases before the bowtie2 alignments. The k-mer scan always reads them whole.

param.name: shred_length
param.label: Length of the pieces (shred_length)
param.help: Length of the pieces of the sequences longer than shred_max_length: without overlap for reads, half overlapping for an assembly.

section.name: strain
section.title: Strain identity
section.help: Strain identity database section of nextflow.config. The strain identity database (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, 1,172 strains, yeast_db) and its reference genome (panel_reference, S288C R64-1-1) are installed on the Galaxy server.

param.name: kmer_max_bases
param.label: Read bases scanned for the strain panel (kmer_max_bases)
param.help: 0 for all of them. The cap is in bases, not reads, because coverage decides whether a site is called. Scanning everything costs about 90 s for 275 Mb. For a much larger genome or a very deep run, 300000000 gives about 25x on a 12 Mb genome.

param.name: kmer_min_depth
param.label: Minimal k-mer depth of a panel site (kmer_min_depth)
param.help: Number of panel k-mer observations required before a site is called. Below it, the site is reported as not covered, never as carrying the reference allele. Set to 1 for an assembly.

param.name: strain_error_rate
param.label: Error rate of the strain scoring (strain_error_rate)
param.help: Assumed probability that a called allele disagrees with the true strain: sequencing error, culture drift and panel error together. Raising it makes the ranking less confident, it does not change the order.

param.name: marker_min_depth
param.label: Minimal depth of the native marker genes (marker_min_depth)
param.help: Number of well mapped reads (mapping quality 20 or more) needed at a position of a native marker gene before it is read. Below it, the position is unknown, never the reference. Set to 1 for an assembly.

param.name: min_concordance
param.label: Minimal concordance of the strain call (min_concordance)
param.help: If the best strain matches less than this fraction of its expected alleles, the sample is reported as unassigned rather than forced onto the closest strain: this is what catches a strain absent from the database.

section.name: output_options
section.title: Outputs
section.help: The strain identity report is the main result. The report and result folder dataset always contains the whole result folder: its links work in Galaxy and its download button gives a zip of the folder.

param.name: tables
param.label: Result tables as a collection
param.help: The .tsv files of the tsv folder of the results (strain_ranking.tsv, site_calls.tsv, marker_genotype.tsv, tool_coverage.tsv...) as a list collection, to analyze them with other Galaxy tools.

param.name: zip
param.label: Result folder as a separate zip dataset
param.help: Same content as the download of the report and result folder dataset.

param.name: params
param.label: Parameter file (optional)
param.help: JSON object {"parameter": "value"} of nextflow.config parameters, e.g., {"min_concordance": "0.85"}. Its values replace those of the form, to reuse a set of parameters. The input files, the strain identity database, the execution parameters (Local / Cluster execution section of nextflow.config) and the output location cannot be set.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Runs the lab_strain_watch_ Nextflow pipeline on the sequences of a single sample of a laboratory yeast strain (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*), reads or assembly, to check its identity ("is this tube really the strain written on its label?"):
- the most probable strain among the 1,172 strains of the strain identity database, or "unassigned" if none fits well enough, - the mating type (MATa, MATalpha or MATa/alpha), - the genotype of the native marker genes (URA3, HIS3, LEU2, TRP1, LYS2, ADE2, MET15, CAN1, ARG4, LEU5), - the status of the mitochondrial genome (rho+, rho- or rho0), hence whether the strain is expected to grow on glycerol, - the laboratory tool elements present (plasmids, cassettes, drug resistance markers, tags, promoters...).
The form recapitulates the nextflow.config file of the pipeline: same sections, one field per parameter, with the name of the parameter in parentheses, so that the documentation of the pipeline (README and nextflow.config) applies. The strain identity database and the execution parameters (Local / Cluster execution section) are set by the Galaxy server.
.. _lab_strain_watch: https://github.com/lab-strain-watch/lab_strain_watch
-----
**Inputs**
- Sample sequences (fastq_path): one or several files of a single sample (FASTQ, FASTA, GenBank, EMBL, plain or compressed, BAM, SAM, CRAM, or a zip archive), forward and reverse reads, a paired collection, or a run accession (SRA, ENA, DDBJ). - Kind of sequences (seq_kind) and molecule (seq_molecule): reads or assembly, DNA or RNA. - Parameter file (optional): a JSON object {"parameter": "value"} of nextflow.config parameters, which replaces the values of the form.
-----
**Outputs**
- *strain identity report*: the main result, an HTML report with the decision (strain called and the agreement of the mating type, native markers and tool elements with its documented genotype), the warnings, the strain ranking, the tool elements, the native marker genes and the mitochondrial genome. - *report and result folder*: the HTML report of the run (parameters, summary of the database used, warnings). This dataset also contains the whole result folder of the pipeline (tsv and reports folders, see the OUTPUT section of the README), so that the links of the report work in Galaxy. **To save the result folder, click on the download button of this dataset: you get a zip of the folder.** - *tables* (optional): the .tsv files of the tsv folder, as a list collection, for further analyses in Galaxy. - *result folder (zip)* (optional): the result folder as a separate zip dataset.
The results stay in the history: they can also be exported to a storage configured in the Galaxy server (Export datasets).
-----
**Duration**
The whole pipeline runs inside a single Galaxy job: from a few minutes for an assembly to about an hour for a whole-genome sequencing run, plus the waiting time of the job, and longer the first time on a server, which pulls the container images of the pipeline.
